title.en: Describe the water canal system of sponges
Explain cnidoblasts, polyp, medusa and metagenesis

say.en: A bath sponge was once an animal pumping sea water through its body. A jellyfish can sting a swimmer, and a comb jelly glows in the dark sea. In this lesson: Describe the water canal system of sponges.
Explain cnidoblasts, polyp, medusa and metagenesis.
State the features of ctenophores.

body.en: *Sponges* are pore-bearing, mostly marine, asymmetrical animals at the cellular level. Water enters through tiny pores called ostia into the central spongocoel and leaves through the osculum. Collar cells or choanocytes line the spongocoel and canals. Digestion is intracellular. The skeleton is of spicules or spongin fibres. Sponges are hermaphrodite and develop through a larval stage. Examples: Sycon, Spongilla (freshwater) and Euspongia (bath sponge).
body.kn: ಸ್ಪಂಜುಗಳು ರಂಧ್ರಯುಕ್ತ, ಅಸಮಮಿತಿಯ, ಕೋಶ ಮಟ್ಟದ ಪ್ರಾಣಿಗಳು. ನೀರು ಆಸ್ಟಿಯಾ ಮೂಲಕ ಸ್ಪಂಜೋಸೀಲ್‌ಗೆ ಬಂದು ಆಸ್ಕ್ಯುಲಮ್ ಮೂಲಕ ಹೊರಹೋಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಕಾಲರ್ ಕೋಶಗಳು (ಕೊಯನೋಸೈಟ್) ಇವೆ.

narration.en: Collar cells (choanocytes) beat their flagella and draw water in through the tiny ostia, into the central spongocoel and out through the osculum. The water brings food and oxygen and carries away wastes; the collar cells trap food particles. Faster beating moves the water through faster.

say.en: A sponge is a vase of cells with a central cavity, the spongocoel.
Water enters through tiny pores, the ostia.
It leaves through the osculum at the top.
Collar cells, the choanocytes, line the spongocoel and keep water moving.
Cnidarians have two body forms: the fixed polyp and the swimming medusa. Obelia alternates: metagenesis.
Ctenophores, the comb jellies, swim with eight rows of comb plates and glow: bioluminescence.

text.en: Cnidoblasts for anchorage, defence and catching prey
Eight rows of ciliated comb plates

explanation.en: Sponges have a water canal system and cellular level of organisation. Cnidarians have cnidoblasts and tissue level organisation. Ctenophores (sea walnuts, comb jellies) swim with comb plates.

say.en: Three simple animal phyla. Sort the animals and their features.

body.en: Cnidarians have stinging cells, cnidoblasts, on the tentacles for defence and capturing prey. They are radially symmetrical, diploblastic, at the tissue level, with a gastro-vascular cavity that opens through a single hypostome. Corals have a skeleton of calcium carbonate. They exist as the sessile polyp (Hydra, Adamsia) and the free-swimming medusa (Aurelia). In Obelia, polyps produce medusae asexually and medusae form polyps sexually: this alternation is metagenesis.
body.kn: ಸೀಲೆಂಟರೇಟ್‌ಗಳ ಸ್ಪರ್ಶಕಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಕುಟುಕು ಕೋಶಗಳು (ನಿಡೋಬ್ಲಾಸ್ಟ್). ಪಾಲಿಪ್ ಮತ್ತು ಮೆಡ್ಯೂಸಾ ಎರಡು ರೂಪಗಳು. ಒಬೀಲಿಯಾದಲ್ಲಿ ಇವು ಪರ್ಯಾಯವಾಗುವುದು ಮೆಟಾಜೆನೆಸಿಸ್.

body.en: Ctenophores, the sea walnuts or *comb jellies*, are marine, radially symmetrical, diploblastic animals at the tissue level. Their body has eight external rows of ciliated comb plates that help in locomotion. Digestion is both extracellular and intracellular. Bioluminescence, the emission of light, is well marked. Sexes are not separate, fertilisation is external and development indirect. Examples: Pleurobrachia and Ctenoplana.

Comb plates and bioluminescence are the marks of Ctenophora, e.g. Pleurobrachia.
